# Gap register

> A mapping aid for engineers, architects and auditors. It records which controls have checked evidence in which repository and where there are gaps. It is not legal advice, not a conformity assessment and not a statement that any system complies with anything.

Every control that is not `implemented`, with what is missing and who owns the next step. Order: gaps first, then organisational, designed, partial.

| Control | Framework | Status | Owner | What is missing | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `EUAIA-50` Transparency obligations for certain systems | EU AI Act | gap | Product owner of the deployed system | No repository here tells an end user that they are interacting with an AI system, or marks generated content. The reference systems are back-end components with no user interface. | Add a disclosure to every user-facing channel (chat, email, voice) and record where it appears; decide how generated content is marked. |
| `EUAIA-04` AI literacy | EU AI Act | organisational | AI governance lead | Literacy measures are about people: who is trained, on what, and how that is recorded. No repository can show it. | Define role-based AI literacy measures for staff who operate or oversee AI systems and record completion. |
| `EUAIA-17` Quality management system | EU AI Act | organisational | Head of quality | A quality management system is an organisation-wide, documented set of procedures. Supporting engineering practice exists in the platform operating model (change classes, governance cadence, waivers) and in review and CI gates across the repositories. | Decide whether Article 17 applies, and if so write the quality manual and map the engineering gates to it. |
| `EUAIA-26` Obligations of deployers | EU AI Act | organisational | Business owner of the deployed system | Deployer duties are about how an organisation uses a system: assigned overseers, input data quality, monitoring, log retention and informing workers. The approval policy and audit tooling support them. | Name the overseers, set log retention, document monitoring and, where applicable, inform workers and affected people. |
| `EUAIA-73` Reporting of serious incidents | EU AI Act | organisational | Legal and compliance | Reporting to authorities within legal deadlines is a legal and operational process. The incident runbooks give a starting structure. | Define what counts as a serious incident, who decides, the reporting deadlines and the contact route to the market surveillance authority. |
| `ISO42001-A.2.2` AI policy | ISO/IEC 42001:2023 | organisational | Head of AI governance | An AI policy is a management document. Technical policy-as-code exists in several repositories but there is no organisational AI policy here. | Draft the AI policy, have management approve it and communicate it. |
| `ISO42001-A.3.2` AI roles and responsibilities | ISO/IEC 42001:2023 | organisational | Head of AI governance | A responsibility matrix exists for the reference platform; allocation for an organisation is a management decision. | Allocate AI roles to named positions and record them in the management system. |
| `ISO42001-A.5.2` AI system impact assessment process | ISO/IEC 42001:2023 | organisational | Head of AI governance | An impact assessment process is a management procedure with triggers, templates and sign-off. None exists here. | Define the process, the triggers (including substantial modification) and the record format. |
| `ISO42001-A.8.4` Communication of incidents | ISO/IEC 42001:2023 | organisational | Legal and compliance | Deciding how and when incidents are communicated to interested parties is a management decision. | `ISO42001-A.9.2` Processes for responsible use | ISO/IEC 42001:2023 | organisational | Head of AI governance | Responsible use is defined by organisational processes. Technical enforcement exists in approval policy and default-deny tool policy, which supports those processes. | Define responsible-use processes, then express the enforceable parts as policy files like these. |
| `NIST-MG-4.3` Incidents and errors communicated | NIST AI RMF 1.0 | organisational | Legal and compliance | Communicating incidents to affected parties is an organisational process. Runbooks provide an incident structure; the audit tooling supports reconstruction. | Define who is told what, when, for each incident class, including affected communities. |
| `ISO42001-A.10.3` Suppliers | ISO/IEC 42001:2023 | designed | Vendor management | A design decision and a risk entry. No supplier assessment process, contract controls or supplier review records. | Define supplier assessment criteria and keep a record for each model and data provider. |

| `EUAIA-09` Risk management system | EU AI Act | partial | Model risk lead | No lifecycle risk process for a specific deployed system: no testing against foreseeable misuse for a declared purpose, no residual-risk acceptance record, no review trigger on substantial modification. | Adopt the risk register as a template for each deployed system, add a residual-risk acceptance step and a review trigger on change. |
